title: SRM College of Occupational Therapy Marks World Occupational Therapy Day 2026 with Focus on Addiction Recovery
summary: SRM College of Occupational Therapy, SRMIST, Kattankulathur, celebrated World Occupational Therapy Day 2026 on the theme "Addiction Management: Participation Matters".
body_html:
Chennai, 24 November 2026: SRM College of Occupational Therapy, SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST), Kattankulathur, celebrated World Occupational Therapy Day 2026 on 24 November 2026 at the Hippocrates Auditorium on campus. Held to mark World Occupational Therapy Day, which is observed on 27 October, the programme carried the theme "Addiction Management: Participation Matters" and focused on the role of occupational therapy in addiction management, recovery and rehabilitation.

Academicians, healthcare professionals, occupational therapists, faculty members and students attended the event, which sought to raise awareness of how occupational therapy can help people affected by addiction return to meaningful engagement in their personal, social and working lives.

Dr. T. Mythili, Additional Registrar (MSL), SRMIST, presided over the inaugural function and delivered the presidential address. Speaking on the place of healthcare in restoring dignity and social inclusion, she said, “Whatever the setbacks, the true purpose of healthcare is to help individuals regain their confidence, dignity and sense of inclusion in society. The impact you can create through your profession is truly remarkable. With the growing role of AI, the human touch in healthcare will always remain irreplaceable. I urge every student to recognise the immense opportunities ahead and understand that they have the power to make a meaningful difference in countless lives across the world.”

In his welcome address, Dr. U. Ganapathy Shankar, Dean, SRM College of Occupational Therapy, SRMIST, stressed that participation lies at the heart of rehabilitation. “Occupational Therapy is not merely about restoring physical function; it is about enabling individuals to participate meaningfully in everyday activities, including education, work, family life and community engagement. Our success is measured not by the functions we restore, but by how meaningfully a person participates in daily life. Because participation matters,” he said.

The Chief Guest, Dr. Anil K. Srivastava, Former President of the All India Occupational Therapists' Association and Director of Rehabcare, Lucknow, and Deenbandhu Rehabilitation Center, Ayodhya, called for stronger occupational therapy services in addiction management. He spoke about the profession's role in helping individuals rebuild confidence, restore relationships and resume meaningful occupations, and underlined the importance of professional commitment, collaborative practice and community-based rehabilitation in improving quality of life.

The Guest of Honour and Resource Person, Dr. Lakshmanan. S, Senior Occupational Therapist, Centre for Addiction Medicine, National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences (NIMHANS), Bengaluru, shared insights on addiction management and recovery. He advocated a holistic, person-centred approach built on structured routines, meaningful activities, healthy lifestyles, social participation, evidence-based interventions and interdisciplinary collaboration.

Mrs. Grace Lydia Sarojini D, Vice Principal, SRM College of Occupational Therapy, SRMIST, was also present at the event. Through the celebration, the college reaffirmed its commitment to advancing the profession and to promoting meaningful participation as an essential part of recovery and rehabilitation.
